I've found a security bug in the WASI filesystem host implementation.

*   New WASM test programs must be created at crates/test-programs/src/bin/preview1_file_truncation_readonly.rs and crates/test-programs/src/bin/preview2_file_truncation_readonly.rs. These binaries are compiled by the test infrastructure and their paths are exported as constants PREVIEW1_FILE_TRUNCATION_READONLY, PREVIEW1_FILE_TRUNCATION_READONLY_COMPONENT, and PREVIEW2_FILE_TRUNCATION_READONLY_COMPONENT in the test_programs_artifacts crate.

*   The preview1 WASM test program must locate the preopened directory named 'readonly' (using open_scratch_directory("readonly")), attempt to open the file 'test.txt' with the truncation open-flag (OFLAGS_TRUNC) and read rights only, and verify that the operation fails with the error code ERRNO_PERM. It must also verify that the file contents equal b"truncation test file\n" both before and after the attempted truncation.

*   The preview2 WASM test program must locate the preopened directory named 'readonly' from the preopens list, attempt to open the file 'test.txt' with OpenFlags::TRUNCATE and DescriptorFlags::READ only, and verify that the operation fails with ErrorCode::NotPermitted. It must also verify that the file contents equal b"truncation test file\n" both before and after the attempted truncation.

*   The host WASI filesystem implementation in crates/wasi/src/host/filesystem.rs must treat the truncation open-flag as implying a write operation when checking permissions. Specifically, when OpenFlags::TRUNCATE is present, the OpenMode::WRITE flag must be included in the permission check, so that a file preopened with FilePerms::READ only (without FilePerms::WRITE) causes the open request to be rejected with a permission error.

*   After a WASM program (both Preview 1 and Preview 2 variants) runs against a preopened directory configured with DirPerms::READ | DirPerms::MUTATE and FilePerms::READ (no FilePerms::WRITE), the host-side test verifies that the file 'test.txt' still contains exactly b"truncation test file\n" (i.e., no truncation occurred).

*   Placeholder tests named preview1_file_truncation_readonly must be added to crates/wasi-common/tests/all/async_.rs and crates/wasi-common/tests/all/sync.rs. These are no-op tests that satisfy a build-time macro check (assert_test_exists) and simply print a notice that the feature is not applicable to wasi-common.

Must exit with code 0 (no trap) when all assertions pass.

Must locate the preopened directory with guest path "readonly" from preopens::get_directories(), verify the file "test.txt" contains b"truncation test file\n", attempt to open "test.txt" with OpenFlags::TRUNCATE and DescriptorFlags::READ (no WRITE flag), assert the result is an error equal to ErrorCode::NotPermitted, then verify file contents are still b"truncation test file\n". Must exit cleanly when all assertions pass.

Type: Bug fix (implementation)
Name: open_at / path_open truncation permission check
Location: crates/wasi/src/host/filesystem.rs
Description: When OpenFlags::TRUNCATE is present in a file-open request, the OpenMode::WRITE flag must be OR-assigned into the open_mode variable used for permission checking. This ensures that a file opened with the truncation flag requires FilePerms::WRITE, causing the request to be rejected with a permission error (ErrorCode::NotPermitted / ERRNO_PERM) when only FilePerms::READ was granted.


**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.
I'll start by exploring the repository structure to understand the conventions used.

## Summary

I implemented the security fix and its supporting test infrastructure across four source areas (leaving all verification-patched test files untouched):

**1. Host fix — `crates/wasi/src/host/filesystem.rs`** (the actual bug)

In `open_at`, when `OpenFlags::TRUNCATE` was set, the code called `opts.truncate(true).write(true)` on the OS-level options but never added `OpenMode::WRITE` to the `open_mode` used for the WASI permission check. So a file preopened with `FilePerms::READ` only could still be truncated. The fix:

```rust
if oflags.contains(OpenFlags::TRUNCATE) {
    opts.truncate(true).write(true);
    open_mode |= OpenMode::WRITE;   // <-- truncation implies write
}
```

Now the existing check `!d.file_perms.contains(FilePerms::WRITE) && open_mode.contains(OpenMode::WRITE)` correctly rejects the request with `ErrorCode::NotPermitted`.

**2. `crates/test-programs/src/bin/preview1_file_truncation_readonly.rs`** — opens the `readonly` preopen, asserts `test.txt` contents equal `b"truncation test file\n"`, attempts `path_open` with `OFLAGS_TRUNC` + `RIGHTS_FD_READ`, asserts `ERRNO_PERM`, then re-verifies contents unchanged.

**3. `crates/test-programs/src/bin/preview2_file_truncation_readonly.rs`** — finds the `readonly` preopen by name, verifies contents, attempts `open_at` with `OpenFlags::TRUNCATE` + `DescriptorFlags::READ`, asserts `ErrorCode::NotPermitted`, re-verifies contents.

**4. Placeholders in `crates/wasi-common/tests/all/{sync,async_}.rs`** — required no-op `preview1_file_truncation_readonly` tests so the auto-generated `foreach_preview1!(assert_test_exists)` build-time check keeps compiling (the feature is preview2-specific and not applicable to wasi-common).

**On the CRITICAL note:** I did not touch the verification-patched behavioral tests in `crates/wasi/tests/` or the top-level `tests/`. The wasi-common placeholders are a distinct, explicitly-required build-plumbing item (without them the wasi-common test crate fails to compile once the new `preview1_*` binary exists), and the task called them out specifically — so I added them there and nowhere else. If your verification patch also adds those two placeholder functions, they would collide; let me know and I'll remove mine.
